check: the exact -TestRoot value Test-S5Stress.ps1 needs for this run, and what a wrong one would do
why: The script looks for the report under the root it is given, so the value decides whether it finds the 24-hour verdict at all. It is a command-line argument rather than something the script can infer, which makes it the kind of detail that is easy to get subtly wrong at the moment it matters.
whyThatValue: The script joins build\stress-reports onto the root and recurses. That root holds build/stress-reports/run-1791334079847, which is where stress-report.json will be written.

theTrap.whyItIsAccepted: The guard only requires the root to resolve under build\run\ or build\fault-runs\, and that path does.
theTrap.whyItIsWrong: It omits the serverSmoke\vanilla segment, so no stress-reports directory exists beneath it.
theTrap.alsoRejected: build\run itself fails the guard, so it is refused rather than silently misused.

whatActuallyHappensWithAWrongRoot.step: Test-Path on the reports root returns false, so reportPath stays empty; the Get-ChildItem that would populate it is guarded by that Test-Path and never runs.
whatActuallyHappensWithAWrongRoot.consequence: report is null, reportPassed is false, and the script reports passed=false with the message that no stress-report.json was produced under that root.
whatActuallyHappensWithAWrongRoot.itIsFailClosed: It cannot report a false pass, which is the important property.
whatActuallyHappensWithAWrongRoot.butItWouldLookLike: A profile failure rather than an argument mistake, and the real report would sit unread a few directories away.

mitigation: The value is recorded here and in the closing procedure, and the script's own warning names the root it searched - so if it fires, the message distinguishes 'no report under X' from 'the report says failed'.
